title: Kernel labops afternoon log — Zev
content:
Quick context: afternoon slot to chase the p99 regression after last night's deploy. Feeling fuzzy — capturing everything messy so I don't forget.

Today goals:
- triage the SR-6789 p99 spike (slow batches on 24-token sequences)
- verify whether KV cache change in PR #542 correlates with increased mutex contention
- run a small A/B on batch size 4 vs batch size 2 on the 3090 test rig (local)
- jot down mitigation steps so SRE oncall can roll back quickly if needed

Immediate observations (symptoms):
- p99 token latency up ~15% for short sequences (<=32) on region-nyc-prod-serving group A
- CPU steal spikes on the serving daemon host during high-concurrency (seen 03:14–03:48 UTC)
- logs show occasional "kvCache: miss->warm rebuild" messages for otherwise hot prefixes

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction threshold change combined with small-batch path causes more frequent warms -> higher latency for short sequences.
2) Locking change in PR #542 introduced a hot lock in kv cache get path at high QPS.
3) Kernel scheduling edge-case when many tiny GPU kernels are launched (micro-batching) leading to CPU wait and delayed submission.

Quick checks performed:
- grepped logs for "kvCache: miss->warm" across last 6h (jq + ag). Found correlated bursts with p99 windows.
- instrumented runtime locally to count lock hold times (naive shim): average hold time ~ 120us on dev (previous baseline ~ 20us) — this is concerning.
- recreated traffic in local minicluster with synthetic 80% short sequences traffic: p99 rose when lock hold >50us.

Commands / snippets used (for my future self):
- tail logs: kubectl -n serving logs -l app=runtime -c runtime --since=6h | ag "kvCache: miss->warm" -n
- measure lock times: LD_PRELOAD=./lock-timer.so ./runtime-binary --test-workload
- replay: python tools/replay_workload.py --trace traces/nyc-2026-03-10-shortseq.json --concurrency 120

Experiment plan (this afternoon):
1) A: revert the KV threshold change in a canary build (tag: canary/kv-revert) and run the replay; B: current build. Measure p50/p95/p99 + mutex histogram.
2) If A reduces lock hold times back to ~20us and p99 drops -> root cause likely KV path change.
3) If not, try micro-batch aggregator change: add batching debounce of 1ms to reduce kernel launch frequency.

Concrete TODOs (short):
- [ ] push canary/kv-revert image to staging and run 10-minute replay (owner: me) — target 15:20 PT
- [ ] drop quicklock shim into PR #542 to add tracepoints (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] open SR rollback runbook (owner: Hannah) with exact image tag and healthcheck rollback steps
- [ ] add a short metric for "kv_lock_hold_us" to runtime metrics (follow up with product-metrics)

Blocking / questions:
- Need guidance from infra about whether increasing /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio on the host could affect this (seems unlikely but asked infra slack).
- Is there a scheduled maintenance that would have bumped CPU affinity? (check with release-engineering)

Meeting notes (quick):
- 14:05 sync w/ Aisha: agreed to add tracepoints rather than immediate revert. We'll run both in parallel: tracepoints on current + revert canary.
- 14:30 pinged SRE oncall with the SR link and asked to pause any rolling during the next 30m.

Decisions / safe rollbacks:
- safe rollback plan: deploy canary/kv-revert to 5% traffic -> if p99 improved by >8% and error rate stable -> escalate to 50% then full rollout. If no improvement, revert canary.

Notes to self (detritus):
- check PR #538 for unrelated kernel launch batching tweaks (might interact)
- sometimes nvlink resets show up as transient token spikes; check dmesg last night on the two affected hosts
- file a short post-mortem draft if we confirm a regression root cause (include timeline + metrics + diff)

End-of-slot micro-retro:
- what worked: quick local repro to validate lock timing effect — saved time.
- what didn't: no early metric to show lock hold times in prod. Add this.
- next: get canary running, collect histograms, and then decide on rollback vs fix.

Random brainstorm (future):
- consider moving KV read path to lock-free snapshotting for hot prefixes or per-thread read cache. Candidate follow-up ticket.

-- Zev
